newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Telkom says riding on multimedia boom.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Telkom says riding on multimedia boom.

text.p: Indonesian telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia said on Friday it was riding the country's multimedia and cellular telephone boom to boost earnings.

"The strong growth in mobile cellular services has contributed to a significant increase in earnings...and may form an important source of revenue in the future," Telkom president-director Asman Akhir Nasution told analysts in a conference call.

Telkom, which is also listed in New York and London, announced on Friday it had posted a net profit of 399.0 billion rupiah ($163.9 million) in the first quarter of 1997 against 307.2 billion rupiah in the same year-ago period.
Nasution said the state-controlled firm had beefed up efforts to exploit the opportunities of expected strong growth in the country's multimedia industry.
In the past several months alone, Telkom has launched initiatives to ensure its place in the country's multimedia sector, Nasution said.
Telkom had raised its stake in directory services firm PT Infomedia Nusantara to 20.1 percent from 15 percent from April.

On May 7, the firm signed an agreement to set up another multimedia company, PT Indonusa Telemedia, which would offer services including news on demand, video on demand and home shopping, Nasution said.

Telkom owns a 35 percent stake in Indonusa, which is 20-percent owned by PT Rajawali Citra Televisi Indonesia, the country's privately-owned television station controlled by President Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo.
Private-owned telecommunications firms PT Telekomindo Primabhakti and PT Datakom Asia respectively own 20 percent and 25 percent of Indonusa.
Telkom signed another agreement in May to form multimedia firm PT Multimedia Nusantara, which would offer pay television and other multimedia services, he said.
Telkom has a 31 percent stake in the firm, with the rest owned by state-owned organisations PT Indosat Mega Media and Yayasan TVRI and a privately-owned firm, Nasution said.
On May 13, Telkom signed an agreement to increase its shareholding by 2.46 percent to 27.46 percent in PT Aplikanusa Lintasarta, whose services include the Internet.
Nasution said Telkom had also entered into an agreement with Lockheed Martin of the United States to buy a $85 million satellite to boost its multimedia services.

He said a strong growth in mobile cellular services had boosted earnings by 14.7 billion rupiah from its subsidiaries and affiliates in the first quarter of 1997 against a loss of 3.0 billion rupiah in the same year-ago period.
Telkom has a 22.5 percent stake in the country's top cellular phone firm PT Satelindo and a 42.7 percent stake in the second largest firm, PT Telkomsel.
Total number of cellular phone subscribers in Indonesia was up more than 100 percent to 689,402 as of March 31, 1997 from 272,250 in the same 1996 period, a Telkom official said. ($1=2,435 rupiah)
